note: Found by the derived calls oracle: clojure/core.clj:4748 is `(defmacro fn …)`, so core.clj redefines `fn` as a bootstrap macro, and the CLJ-D39 shadow rule — a local definition wins over the core list — published every `(fn …)` below that line as a call to the file's own var. 212 edges, all wrong. `fn` is a SPECIAL FORM; a file defining it does not turn it into a var. The check belongs BEFORE the shadow rule, not after it, and it is on the whole head rather than a prefix. Pins: `fn` and `loop` are never call targets, and `fnan?` — a name that merely starts with "fn" — is an ordinary var and is.
